newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Keppel Corp sinks to 44-month low.
newsitem.headline: Keppel Corp sinks to 44-month low.

text.p: Shiprepair conglomerate Keppel Corp Ltd sank to a 44-month low of Singapore $8.60 on Tuesday morning dampened by an unexciting earnings outlook for 1997, dealers said.
At 0350 GMT, the Keppel shares were changing hands at S$8.75, up five cents.
The last time Keppel struck these levels was in mid-August 1993. Volume was a brisk 1.8 million shares, including several blocks which crossed at around S$8.80.
"Looking at the share price, there must be some funds selling again. It might be linked to Keppel Land," said a dealer with a local firm.
Keppel Land (KepLand), the property subsidiary of Keppel Corp, also touched a new 1997 low of S$3.98 with more than one million shares traded.
An analyst with a British broking firm said KepLand had more downside as the outlook for Singapore property was not rosy and earnings growth was expected to slow in 1997.
"KepLand is overvalued at these levels. It could go down to around S$3.50," he said.

Analysts said Keppel, usually seen as a proxy to the Singapore economy with its interests ranging from shiprepair to property and banking, had also been falling out of favour with investors in recent months.

"We will see a fall in earnings per share growth. There is going to be a lot of dilution as a bunch of warrants and convertible loanstock will expire in the later part of this year," another analyst said.
